context: Dataset 'edge-cases', full graph: concepts = [attention, bert, elmo, fasttext, glove, gpt 35, gpt 4, gpt 4o, llama 13b, llama 7b, ontology, roberta, seq2seq, tokenization, transformer, word2vec]; edges (a, b, score) = [(bert, roberta, 60), (bert, transformer, 84), (elmo, fasttext, 69), (fasttext, glove, 70), (gpt 35, gpt 4, 88), (gpt 35, gpt 4o, 40), (gpt 4, gpt 4o, 86), (gpt 4o, llama 7b, 0), (llama 7b, llama 13b, 100), (roberta, bert, 90), (seq2seq, attention, 90), (tokenization, tokenization, 100), (transformer, seq2seq, 85), (word2vec, glove, 72)]. Cluster by these rules: an edge is kept when score >= threshold (inclusive); ignore self-loops (a equals b) whatever their score; a pair listed more than once, in either direction, is linked if any of its listings is kept; clusters are the connected components under the kept edges, so A~B and B~C put A, B and C in one cluster even without A~C; a concept with no kept edge is a singleton cluster, and every concept is in exactly one cluster. Sort each cluster's members ascending in Python's default string order (e.g. 'gpt 35' < 'gpt 4', 'llama 13b' < 'llama 7b') and name the cluster by its first member; sort the clusters by name ascending. Output every cluster, singletons included, and echo dataset and threshold from the input.
